result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-032-schema.md, resolving the single confirmation question docs/agents/design/REQ-032.md Sec0/Sec8 item 1 routed to this role: whether registrations.no_show_reason (existing, added by REQ-011's migration apps/bot/drizzle/0001_tired_annihilus.sql, a plain nullable text column with no CHECK) should stay a single free-text column or be split into reason_code (closed enum) + reason_free_text (nullable), for PRD FR-16's partner-factsheet 'why people missed it' aggregation.

Read apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts's current registrations table in full (line 282's exact noShowReason: text("no_show_reason") declaration), apps/bot/drizzle/0001_tired_annihilus.sql (confirming the column's original, unchanged shape since REQ-011), docs/agents/design/REQ-031-schema.md (the topic_votes type-decision precedent's reasoning style, reused here), and .claude/agents/data-designer.md in full. Grepped apps/bot/src for no_show_reason/noShowReason: confirmed exactly one file references it today -- apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts itself (the declaration and its comment) -- no handler, domain function, job, or test reads or writes it yet, matching CODE-DESIGNER's own finding.

DECISION: keep the single column exactly as CODE-DESIGNER's design already assumes (REQ-032.md Sec1.1). No schema change, no migration, for REQ-032. Reasoning (REQ-032-schema.md Sec2, weighed on the merits, not a rubber stamp):

1. The aggregation concern is real but the single column does not actually block it -- a standard CASE WHEN no_show_reason = ANY(the five literals) THEN no_show_reason ELSE 'other' END, GROUP BY 1 produces exactly the six buckets (five fixed reasons + other) a factsheet line needs, because NoShowReasonCode's five values are canonical, language-invariant, exact-match literals already written verbatim by writeNoShowReason -- not a fragile parse of raw uncontrolled text. The two-column split makes the SQL marginally more direct (GROUP BY reason_code) but that is a smaller benefit than it first appears once the CASE query is written out.

2. No stated requirement calls for the split yet. FR-16's partner factsheet is not REQ-032's scope (REQ-032 implements USER-STORIES D3, capturing the reason -- not the factsheet that later reads it). No REQ-032 acceptance criterion exercises aggregation; AC2 only tests that selecting a reason writes it to registrations.no_show_reason, satisfied either way. Splitting now would shape storage for a requirement not yet drafted, against this role's own mandate not to add a field a stated requirement does not call for.

3. The decisive practical cost: a split is not schema-isolated. CODE-DESIGNER's REQ-032.md design already built RegistrationNoShowContext.noShowReason (one string|null field), the single writeNoShowReason(db, registrationId, reason: string, at: Date) write path shared by both the fixed-code and free-text paths, and an identical 'already answered' gate (context.noShowReason !== null) checked at four separate points (Sec3.4 step3, Sec4.1 step8, Sec4.2 step8, Sec4.3 step7) -- all around one column. Splitting would require CODE-DESIGNER to reshape that already-specified write contract, which is CODE-DESIGNER's domain, not this role's to impose unilaterally.

4. The door stays open, cheaply, for later: if a future factsheet requirement's own DATA-DESIGNER pass determines a split is genuinely needed, it is a small additive migration then (ADD COLUMN + one-time backfill via the same CASE expression), non-destructive to any row written under this design in the meantime. Waiting costs nothing; splitting now buys a marginally simpler future query at the cost of reopening an already-complete design today.

Resolved column definition (unchanged, no edit to schema.ts needed): no_show_reason text, nullable, no default, no CHECK -- nullable/no-default because NULL means 'not asked or asked-and-unanswered' (REQ-032.md Sec2 design question 2 already treats these identically; the once-only-send guarantee lives in notification_ledger's UNIQUE(registration_id, kind), not on this column); no CHECK because the same column legitimately holds either one of five canonical literals or arbitrary free text, and a CHECK...IN(...) cannot express that union without rejecting valid free-text answers; text not pgEnum because, unlike admission/event_format/event_status/check_in_method (genuinely closed sets holding ONLY their enumerated values), this column must also hold values outside any fixed set.

Keys/relationships/cascade: unaffected -- no FK, no unique index, no new cascade rule. Extended (not resolved) REQ-031-schema.md Sec8 item 1's open S13 anonymization question to this column: whether free-text no_show_reason answers (the 'other' path) should be included in a future anonymization routine's blanked-field list is left open, since no such routine exists yet in this codebase to decide it against.

Confirmed BACKEND-DEV's Step 2 action: nothing schema-side. No migration, no schema.ts edit, no drizzle-kit generate run. REQ-032.md's own domain/handler/job/i18n file list (Sec1-Sec5) is buildable as-is against the existing column.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-032-schema.md Sec7 open question 1: whether a future partner-factsheet requirement should split registrations.no_show_reason into reason_code/reason_free_text is deliberately left open, not resolved either way -- Sec2.4 states the split remains cheap and non-destructive to add later, additively, once that requirement exists to specify its exact needs.

docs/agents/design/REQ-032-schema.md Sec7 open question 2: whether free-text no_show_reason values (the 'other' answer) should be included in a future S13 anonymization routine's blanked-field list -- extends REQ-031-schema.md Sec8 item 1's identical open question (there, for feedback.liked/improve/topic_votes) to this column; no anonymization routine exists yet in this codebase to decide it against.
